examples.en: I packed butane gas when I went camping.

examples.ko: 부탄가스가 떨어져서 불을 켤 수 없어요.
examples.en: The butane ran out, so I can't light the stove.
I put a butane canister into the portable gas stove.
Butane canisters are dangerous if kept close to a fire.
I bought four cans of butane at the supermarket.

examples.ko: 다 쓴 부탄가스는 분리배출 안내를 보고 버리세요.
examples.en: Check the recycling instructions before throwing away empty butane cans.

explain: 캠핑이나 집에서 휴대용 가스레인지에 끼워 쓰는 작은 통을 보통 이렇게 불러요. '부탄가스 한 통'처럼 '통'으로 세요. 열이나 불 근처에서는 위험하니까 보관할 때 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: People usually use this name for the small canister that fits into a portable gas stove, whether camping or at home. You count them with '통', as in '부탄가스 한 통'. They are dangerous near heat or fire, so storage needs care.

examples.en: He made exercise his outlet for stress.
Smoke is rising from the volcano's vent.
Children need an outlet to spend their energy.
Writing is the outlet for my feelings.
It is dangerous to block the vent where the gas comes out.

examples.ko: 분출구 없이 화를 참기만 하면 병이 나요.
examples.en: If you only hold in your anger with no outlet, you will get sick.

explain: 가스나 용암이 나오는 구멍을 뜻하기도 하지만, 말할 때는 '감정의 분출구', '스트레스의 분출구'처럼 쌓인 마음을 풀 수 있는 방법이나 곳으로 많이 써요. 보통 '분출구가 필요하다', '분출구를 찾다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It can mean a hole where gas or lava comes out, but in conversation it is mostly used as in '감정의 분출구' or '스트레스의 분출구', meaning a way or place to let out built-up feelings. Common patterns are '분출구가 필요하다' and '분출구를 찾다'.

examples.en: The restroom was so unclean that I did not want to use it.

examples.ko: 음식을 불결한 손으로 만지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not touch food with unclean hands.

examples.ko: 주방이 불결하면 식중독이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the kitchen is unsanitary, food poisoning can happen.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 위생이 불결해 보여서 그냥 나왔어요.
examples.en: The hygiene at this restaurant looked bad, so I just left.
Throw away anything that was stored in an unsanitary way.

examples.ko: 시장 바닥이 불결하다는 말을 들었는데 사실은 깨끗했어요.
examples.en: I heard the market floor was dirty, but it was actually clean.

explain: '더럽다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 위생이나 청결을 말하는 상황에 어울려요. 반대말은 '청결하다'예요. '지저분하다'는 어수선한 것에도 쓰지만 '불결하다'는 위생에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '더럽다' and fits situations about hygiene and cleanliness. Its opposite is '청결하다'. '지저분하다' can also mean messy, but '불결하다' focuses on hygiene.

examples.en: I found something foreign in my food and complained to the shop.
Something got into my eye, and my tears flowed.
The filter strains out impurities.
There was some foreign matter settled at the bottom of the cup.
Something got stuck inside and the machine stopped.

examples.ko: 제품에서 이물질을 발견하면 바로 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If you find foreign matter in the product, please tell us right away.

explain: 음식, 눈, 기계처럼 있으면 안 되는 곳에 들어간 것을 말해요. '이물질이 들어가다', '이물질이 나오다', '이물질이 끼다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 먼지나 머리카락처럼 구체적인 이름을 말할 때도 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to something that has gotten into a place where it shouldn't be, such as food, an eye or a machine. It is used in '이물질이 들어가다', '이물질이 나오다' and '이물질이 끼다'. In daily talk people often name the specific thing, like dust or a hair.

en: be maintained; be overhauled; be put in order

examples.en: The park paths have been newly redone.

examples.ko: 차가 잘 정비돼 있어서 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: The car is well maintained, so I feel safe.
Once the rules are put in order, confusion will decrease.
Many people exercise along the redeveloped riverside.
All planes are inspected before departure.
It took several years for the system to be put in order.

explain: 정비하다의 피동이에요. 길, 시설, 제도가 정리되고 새로워졌다는 말로 뉴스에 많이 나와요. '정비된 도로'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로도 써요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '정비하다'. It appears a lot in the news for roads, facilities, or systems that have been tidied up and renewed. It also works as a modifier, as in '정비된 도로'.

examples.en: The soldiers divided the ammunition into boxes.
The ammunition was almost gone on the battlefield.
The warehouse is piled full of ammunition.
A truck loaded with ammunition drove past slowly.

examples.ko: 병사들이 남은 탄약을 하나씩 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: The soldiers counted the remaining ammunition one by one.

examples.ko: 탄약 보관소에는 아무나 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Not just anyone can enter an ammunition depot.

explain: 탄약은 총알과 포탄을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 써요. 총알 하나는 '총알'이라고 해요. 군대 이야기나 뉴스에서 주로 나오고 '탄약이 떨어지다', '탄약을 보급하다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: This word covers bullets and shells together as a group. A single bullet is '총알'. It shows up in military talk and the news, in phrases like '탄약이 떨어지다' (run out of ammunition) and '탄약을 보급하다' (supply ammunition).

examples.en: The road was flooded from a burst water pipe.
The hospital said it was a ruptured eardrum.
There was an accident caused by a tire blowout.
A ruptured blood vessel is very dangerous.

examples.ko: 배관이 오래되면 파열이 일어날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If pipes get old, they can burst.
A gas pipe rupture occurred during construction.

explain: 파열은 물건이나 몸 안의 무언가가 압력 때문에 터져서 찢어지는 거예요. 수도관, 혈관, 고막, 타이어에 자주 써요. 불이나 큰 소리가 나는 '폭발'과는 달라서 터진 부분이 갈라지거나 새어 나오는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 파열 is when something under pressure splits open, such as a water pipe, blood vessel, eardrum or tire. It differs from 폭발 (explosion): the focus is on a tear or leak, not a blast.

examples.en: All food past its expiration date gets thrown out.

examples.ko: 오래된 서류는 일 년 뒤에 폐기됐어요.
examples.en: The old documents were disposed of a year later.
That plan was finally scrapped at the meeting.

examples.ko: 개인 정보는 사용 후에 바로 폐기돼야 해요.
examples.en: Personal information must be destroyed right after use.
I saw defective products being discarded for the first time.

examples.ko: 법안이 폐기되면 처음부터 다시 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: If the bill is scrapped, it has to be drafted again from scratch.

explain: 폐기되다는 필요 없어진 물건이나 서류, 계획이 버려지거나 없어질 때 써요. 음식, 서류, 법안, 정책처럼 공식적으로 처리되는 것에 어울려요. 일상에서 물건을 버릴 때는 '버리다'를 쓰고, 폐기는 회사나 뉴스에서 더 많이 들어요.
explain_en: 폐기되다 is used when things that are no longer needed, such as items, documents, or plans, are disposed of or dropped. It suits things handled officially, like food, paperwork, bills, and policies. For throwing out everyday items Koreans say '버리다', and 폐기 shows up more at companies and in the news.
